newsitem.title: USA: Former Congressman Charles Hayes dies.
newsitem.headline: Former Congressman Charles Hayes dies.

text.p: Charles Hayes, a one-time stockyards union official who represented Chicago's South Side in Congress for nearly 10 years, has died, his family said Wednesday.

Hayes, 79, was elected to the House in 1983 to fill the balance of Harold Washington's term when Washington was elected mayor of Chicago. He served in the House until he was defeated by Bobby Rush in a 1992 Democratic primary following a redistricting.

A native of Cairo, Illinois, Hayes worked in Chicago's once-booming stockyards, rising through the ranks of various meat cutting unions. He was international vice president of the United Food and Commercial Workers Union from 1979 to 1983 and a long-time meat packing union congressional lobbyist before that.
Hayes died at a Chicago area hospital Tuesday evening, the announcement said.
